attributes.cardDescription: A batched walk through the warehouse — one oversized item at a time, with keyboard-wedge barcode scanning that works with real hardware.
attributes.readMe:
## Pick List

Batching is the point: the same SKU picked once can serve three orders, so `PickItemField.orderNumbers` is plural and the picker is told the total to grab.

The route is a plain sort of bin labels, and `routeOrder()` says why: bins are named so that sorting them lexically walks the aisles in order. That is a property of how bins are labelled, not an optimisation this card invents — calling it a solver would overclaim.

The isolated view is the mobile pick walk: **one item at a time**, oversized, because it is read at arm's length in an aisle by someone holding a box. A USB barcode scanner is a keyboard that types fast and presses Enter, so handling Enter on a text input supports real hardware with no device integration at all — and a scan that does not match the current item says so rather than silently advancing.

Picks persist through `store.patch`, which replaces arrays wholesale, so the whole item list is re-serialized on each write. With no store present (prerender, a read-only surface) the walk renders as a plan and offers no buttons that would silently do nothing.

### Example

`PK-2026-0031` is mid-walk: one line picked, two to go, batched across two orders. `PK-2026-0030` is complete.

### Non-goals

No wave picking or sort-to-order. Grouping many orders into a wave and sorting items back to orders at the packing station is v1.1 in the source spec.
